title: a type-0/1 residue may end past one channel's blocksize/2, so a one-channel submap adds into the next channel's residue
consumer: libavcodec/vorbisdec.c:681-683 (setup) and :1359-1364 (type-1 write) at the fix's parent
object: vc->channel_residues, one av_malloc(blocksize[1] / 2 * channels floats) at libavcodec/vorbisdec.c:952, carved per submap by ch_res_ptr (:1481, :1560-1562)
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the block is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: an end validated against all channels' worth of samples for a per-channel decode
allocator_layer: FFmpeg's own carve of one allocation: the block is the platform's calloc/malloc (as in ../plain-heap-repros, so the allocation bound the arms enforce is real and exact), and the regions are pointer arithmetic on it, exactly as upstream writes it, through shared/driver.c's ffc_carve().
fidelity: real carve arithmetic, model consumer. The block size and every region offset are upstream's expressions at the fix's parent, evaluated at the parameters named in case.c; the consumer is reduced to the stores or loads that cross, the first crossing access going through the labelled probe and the rest of the unreduced overshoot recorded as `extent`. The fixed arm models the fix's own change, including any change to the allocation.
nested_why: the crossed region was carved out of one allocation by FFmpeg's own pointer arithmetic, and the case CHECKs that the whole unreduced overshoot stays inside that allocation, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- the object is FFmpeg's carve, one layer inside malloc: NESTED.

live_proof: read from the PINNED source, two-sided, never from ancestry: LIVE, by reading the pinned source, two-sided, and adversarially audited (claim-auditor, 2026-10-09); NOT demonstrated on a stream. The per-type end check this fix added (`res_setup->type == 2 ? ... : 1`) occurs 0 times at n9.0.1: it was removed by 0a266cb55a (2014), and `git log -G'(vr|res_setup)->end' 0a266cb55a..n9.0.1 -- libavcodec/vorbisdec.c` is empty while the same query over all history lists both commits. The setup check left (n9.0.1:libavcodec/vorbisdec.c:724-725) bounds begin <= end and the partition count only. The one runtime bound is `max_output = (ch - 1) * vlen + vr->end` against `ch_left * vlen` (:1425-1449), which for a one-channel submap with two channels left accepts an end of up to 2 * vlen, and the type-0/1 loops (:1482-1506) then write vec[voffs] up to begin + ptns_to_read * partition_size - 1, into the next channel's slice of channel_residues (one av_malloc_array, :1019) and never past it. The Vorbis I spec, section 8.6.2, has the decoder clamp residue_end to blocksize/2 for formats 0 and 1, so such a stream is LEGAL and a conforming decoder truncates. Conditions: a type-0/1 residue on a submap with fewer channels than remain, begin + ptns_to_read * partition_size > vlen, and a neighbour whose floor is used (an unused one is cleared at :1743-1745 before the MDCT). The audit refined the history: the 2012 check bounded end by blocksize[1]/2 while the write uses the CURRENT block's vlen, so short-block packets could cross even while it stood. What would settle it dynamically: a 2-channel stream with two one-channel submaps whose first residue is type 1 with end = 2 * vlen, decoded by an instrumented n9.0.1, against the same stream with end = vlen. A fix-reversal: the pre-fix carve or consumer is reconstructed, the convention at ../../memcached/allocator-repros/README.md:132-135.
